entries.words: Many newcomers ask that. I am no teacher.

Thorn is the northern border city of the saltrice fields. The Tear road runs from it into Morrowind. House Dres once raided it for slaves and profited from its rice. Today the Thorn Ash-Reed Accord argues over who holds title to the fields.

Hissmir is a pilgrimage xanmeer, a stepped stone pyramid of the old Argonians, in southern Shadowfen. Outsiders and Argonians with no Hist can commune with the Hist there by passing its trials. Root Stewards run the trials and cannot refuse anyone who comes.
The priests of Sithis made blood offerings at the Teeth before the Duskfall. The Clutch of Nisswo still keeps the stones in repair. No sacrifices are made there now.

Shells and Stones is a gambling game played on a marked reed mat at ferry stages. Boat crews play it through the evenings in their crews' house. They stake things on it, even the best bunk. The winner keeps the stake.

Sithis is Raj-Sithis the Changer, First Creator and Final Destroyer, the void god of change. Argonian priests teach that death and loss are its work, so a death is a change, to be mourned and then released.

The Nisswo are the priests of Sithis, the void god of change. They travel so that each village hears many readings of the faith. They keep no single doctrine and no central rule, so no Nisswo can settle a dispute for the whole province.

Gideon is the western frontier city, the first settlement on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil. Its courts still work, so an Owing made there is a paper contract that can be contested in court. Most of its people are Argonian.
A Hist is a great tree with a mind of its own. It is older than the races of men and mer. All the Hist share one mind through their roots. Argonians hatch beside one, drink its sap and listen to it.

Helstrom is the capital of the Argonian interior, a city grown into a Hist grove. The native armies withdrew there after the Battle of Argonia. The Empire chose not to besiege it. No army has ever taken the city.

Ojel is the Argonian word for outsiders. It is a plain word and carries no insult. Lukiul is the slur that the An-Xileel coined for Argonians who hatched outside Black Marsh. Those Argonians cannot hear the Hist.

A tree-minder tends a village's Hist and speaks for it. The minder reads the Hist's signs and will. It feels when the eggs or the tribe are in trouble. The Many-Root Conclave sends minders out to the villages and keeps the trees.

The Many-Root Conclave is an order of Hist stewards. Its minders keep the trees. They see that each tree is asked for its consent. A minder tends one Hist and reads its signs and its will. The Conclave sends minders out to the villages.

The Veiled Reed is the covert office of the An-Xileel, the nativist government of Argonia. It guards the province against its enemies by secrecy and coercion. Its factors travel the interior as the Reed's agents.

The Panther Race is the river that comes down from Cyrodiil. It crosses into easternmost Blackwood and then forks by Greenspring and Helstrom. Its frogs have a chirp that musicians prize. The Pantherfish is a prized catch.

Greenspring is a spring village on the way to Helstrom, where travellers stop for water and a bed. The spring water is free and can be drunk unboiled, which is rare in the region. Salt is reaching the spring. The village blames the salt works upstream.

Chasepoint is a road stage on the coast road, built by the Legion and kept now by wreck-salvage families. Salvage rights there are hereditary. The families dry recovered rope in the old stable. Two families each claim the keeper's office.

Lilmoth is the southern port, built over shallow water, so large ships anchor out and small boats carry the cargo ashore. A council of merchants rules it. The flying city Umbriel destroyed it in 4E 48. It was rebuilt smaller.

The Reed-Sail Compact is the guild of boat crews, routes and ferries. It runs the boats on the rivers and the coast. Pirates called the Salt-Teeth sail inside the Compact, so a crew's name can cover a raider.

The Counted Lots are the numbered pearl beds off the Archon coast. Diver families hold each lot by inheritance. The deep lots pay best and kill divers. The tally book records both the pay and the deaths.

Archon is the eastern port and the province's legal harbour, with marsh to the north of the city and beaches to the south. Pilot families bring ships in through the estuary approach. The harbour authority's power stops at the headland.

Portdun Mont is a pilots' village on the rise above a beach landing near the pearl lots. Pilot families are paid to bring ships through the approach. Their monopoly is custom and has no law behind it.

The Chainbreakers are abolitionists who fight the Owing, the debt that binds a person to labour. They audit the ledgers, burn the debts they can prove false and carry the bones of the dead home, because a soul returns to its Hist.

Blackrose is a lake city in the south, where three rivers meet. The Rose is its old Imperial prison, a day's march south of the city. Families live in the Rose now. In the old days few who entered ever left.

The Tag House is a shelter on the Prison road, built by the Chainbreakers to receive the bones of Argonians who die in the Rose. The Rose's families release the dead for a carriage charge, which the Chainbreakers pay and record.

The Legion remnant is the garrisons that stayed in Black Marsh when the Empire withdrew. Their heirs count as Legion too. The Legion built the old road stages. Wreck-salvage families keep some of them now.

The Prison road, the Border road and the Mile House are old Imperial roads and a waystation. People still call them by their old names. The Prison road runs toward the Rose. The Tag House stands beside it on a dry rise.

The Owing is debt that binds a person to labour until it is paid. It is the marsh's law where there is no court. It began as a sentence of months of work, but it can now be sold and passed down, so a person can be born owing.

Naga are a tall adder-like breed of Argonian. Most of the marsh's brigands are tribeless Naga, who belong to no tribe. Many rob the tracks while merchants walk them. Cut-Rope's raiders are one band of them.

The An-Xileel are the nativist government of Argonia. They began as a party in the Oblivion Crisis that drove the Empire out of Black Marsh. They want the province free of Imperial ways. They coined the slur lukiul for Argonians who lived under those ways.

A Hist is a tree with a mind, older than any people. The eggs lie in a clutch near its roots. On the naming day, each hatchling drinks its sap. The sap shapes its body and scales for life. The sap is our blood and soul. When we die, the spirit goes home to its Hist. The tree-minder reads the Hist's signs and tells the tribe how the clutch fares.

The Cut Circle is a long stilt hall over still water at a lagoon's edge, within a day of Helstrom. One walk on piles leads in from the land. The Unbound Root, a movement that holds the Hist above every law, preaches there in the open.

Alten Corimont is a river port in eastern Shadowfen, on a waterway that runs out to the sea. Argonian pirates and smugglers run the place. They take no side in anyone's war. Any crew may tie up at its docks. The dredging gangs of the lower channel are hired out of those docks.

Alten Meerhleel is a trade port and floating village north-west of Lilmoth. A harbormaster built it in the Second Era so that the swamp tribes could trade with outsiders. The tribes complained that it stood too close to the swamp. To quiet them he built a court north of the docks.

The Archeins are Argonian families who served the slavers. Under the Empire, they ran serf villages and advised the governors of the coast. Other Argonians hate them for it, because they sold their own people and worked the land for foreigners. Tribes forgive one another a great deal, but they have not forgiven this.

Argonia is the name that Black Marsh took when it left the Empire, in the first years of the Fourth Era. It is a marsh country with no emperor over it. Its rulers come from inside the marsh. The An-Xileel are its government.

The Argonians are the lizard-folk who are native to Black Marsh. Their own word for themselves is Saxhleel. An Argonian hatches from an egg beside a Hist tree. The tree's sap shapes the body for life, so every tribe looks a little different. Most Argonians have a natural gift for magic and for stealth.

The Battle of Argonia was fought in the First Era, in the year 2811. It broke the last organised Argonian army. Those who lived marched into the interior and settled at Helstrom. The Emperor of that time would not send soldiers in after them.
The Blackguards are Argonian pirates and brigands of the south coast. They descend from the inmates of Blackrose Prison, the old Imperial jail. They are the largest band of criminals in Murkmire.

Blackwood is the hilly country in the west of Black Marsh. The Blackwood Road climbs through it to Cyrodiil. The people of its hills stay close to their own tree's roots and show little curiosity about strangers. They do like a riddle.

Bog iron is iron that the marsh makes by itself. Water seeps through the ground and leaves a crust of iron in the clay. The Bog Iron Workings lies below the road. The crews there cut that crust into cakes and smelt the cakes in a clay furnace.

Bones-And-Tools is a hollow deep in the jungle, under the layer of roots. It has one mouth that a creature could defend. A creature has made its lair there. It has dragged in what it took. Families who once foraged that way now live at the hiring camp, about a kilometre east. Any of them will tell a stranger why at length.
Bretic means of the Bretons. The Bretons are a human people of the west, from far beyond the marsh. To an Argonian a Breton traveller is an ojel, an outsider. The word is meant plainly.

The Bright-Throats are a tribe of Murkmire who breed horse-lizards and welcome outsiders. Their village has hatching pools and a tree-minder. They seal an alliance with a bonding ceremony and a feast. A ceremony that is called off is a break between peoples.

The Broke Column is what is left of a Legion column. When the Legion was recalled it never paid these men. Their sons and grandsons still live in a camp on a bench in the hills above the Mile House track.

Claywater is a stop in two halves, set at one ford. The station half on one bank is built of timber and stone. The landing half across the water is mud and thatch. Each bank charges a traveller for its own half of the stop.

The College of Whispers is a society of discreet mages chartered by the Empire. They summon Daedra and raise the dead. They know more about Umbriel than any other body. The College has no hall in Argonia. A College scholar who comes looking for the dead of Umbriel is robbing graves.

The Cyrodilic Collections is a society of antiquarians from the Empire. It digs up Argonian relics, repairs them and offers to return them to the marsh. Its great hope is a museum of Argonian history in Argonia. That museum has not been built. Argonians argue over whether a find belongs in a museum or with its tribe.

The Dunmer are the dark elves of Morrowind, the land north of the marsh. House Dres, one of their great houses, grew powerful by raiding Argonians for slaves. It ran that trade for centuries. Morrowind ended slavery long ago, but the grievance on the marsh side runs two hundred years deep.

A clutch is the eggs of one family, laid together in a warm place near the roots of the Hist. The egg-tender looks after the clutch until the eggs hatch. The tender reads to the eggs, plays the flute to them and writes down each egg's parents, hatch day and star sign. A family guards its clutch because the eggs depend on the Hist beside them.
Fish-Eye Rye is a liquor from Hissmir, the pilgrimage xanmeer in southern Shadowfen. A drinker plugs the nostrils before the first swallow.

Gang Ground is the camp where the families of a dredging gang live. It stands on firm ground between the Border road and the marsh. It is about forty years old. The top terrace is dry enough for a hatching shed. The gang's clutch lies in it. The families stay because the eggs are there.

Hist sap is the juice of a Hist tree. The Argonians call it the tree's soul. A hatchling drinks it on the naming day. The rites of coming of age call for it again. Too much of it poisons even an Argonian. The mouth turns gold, the scales thicken like bark and visions come unasked. To an outsider it is a drug that stirs up bloodlust.

House Dres was the great house of the Dunmer that built its wealth on Argonian slaves. The Dres remnant are the claimants who survived when the trade was ended. They still pursue what the house once owned in the north.

Imperial means of the Empire in Cyrodiil. The Empire held the coasts and the borders of Black Marsh for a long age and did not hold the deep marsh. It built the old roads, the road stages and the prisons. Then it withdrew. Its roads and stages are still here.

The League of Open Water is a body of citizens, merchants and workers who argue for civic standing that does not depend on a tribe or a Hist. They argue over citizenship and property. Its hall is in Gideon, where the courts still work.

The Lighter Flotilla is a floating quarter off the east bank of Lilmoth. Four old hulls that once carried cargo to shore now serve as houses. They lie in a line along one timber pier, with the market rafts on its far side.

Long-Water Hold is the village of a settled Naga tribe in the deep marsh. It stands on firm ground on the main poling route of the inner swamp, with a landing deep enough for loaded craft. Its people tend a Hist, villages and fields. They want the road trade. They quarrel with their tribeless kin who rob that road.

Lukiul is a slur for an assimilated Argonian, one who took on Imperial ways. The An-Xileel coined it for Argonians who lived under the Empire. An Argonian hatched outside Black Marsh cannot hear the Hist. The slur lands hardest on those.

The Marsh Charter is a tradition of fighters for hire in Argonia. The Empire's Fighters Guild charter ended with Imperial rule here. The tradition opposes taking on a foreign charter again. The work itself is old. Villages, cities and tribes hired fighters long before any guild came.

Morrowind is the Dunmer province north of Black Marsh. Its dark elves rule it through great houses. One of them raided the marsh for slaves for centuries. Argonian armies marched into Morrowind in the first years of the Fourth Era and sacked Mournhold. Today the border is cold, quiet and resented on both sides.

The Morrowind veterans are Dunmer soldiers from the Accession War, fought in the first years of the Fourth Era. They did not go home when the fighting ended. They stayed in the marsh and live there still.

Murkmire is the southern region of Black Marsh, on Oliis Bay. A dozen tribes or more live in it. No single ruler stands over them. The Naga-Kur rule the deep swamps in the north. Torchbugs light the cypress along the water. The flesh-flies thicken toward the middle.
The Murkwater are a tribe of Murkmire, hunters and trainers. Murkwater is also the name of their village, so a traveller may hear it for either.

The Naga are a tall, adder-like breed of Argonian, seven or eight feet high, with wide mouths full of needle fangs. They live in the deep parts of the marsh. Not every Naga is a brigand. Not every Argonian hates them. The Naga-Kur rule the inner swamps. The tribeless Naga are the robbers of the roads.

The Naga-Kur are the Naga people who rule the inner swamps of Murkmire. They are proud, traditional warriors. They wear the bones of their fallen comrades on their arms. The villages around them fear them. They are cold to outsiders.

A naheesh is an elder of an Argonian tribe, an office beside the tree-minder's. The naheesh carries the tribe's sacred croaks and the secrets of its naming. The people respect the elder greatly, but the office gives no power to rule.

The Night-Reed Chapter is the thieves' guild of Argonia. It is a native guild, not a copy of the one in Cyrodiil. It works the canals, the boats, the flooded districts and the rootworm routes. A new member starts as a lookout.

Nine Bends is a tribe's village built round one Hist tree on a low island, nine bends of river above the port of Alten Corimont. The water there is still fresh. The gang families of the lower channel hatched under that tree. Each year more of the village's adults are away on the downriver roll.

The Turning Path is an order of the Nisswo, the priests of Sithis. It runs the temple called the Teeth of Sithis in Murkmire. Its priests teach about change, endings and mourning. They settle quarrels between villagers.

The North Cut is a road that Imperial surveyors cut north from Stormhold toward the Tear road. They abandoned it after four kilometres. It has no residents. The villagers quarry its stone for their yards. The cut now drains water onto two fields and a hamlet.

The Onkobra is a river that rises near Topal Bay and runs east past Gideon into the middle of the province. The road beside it is muddy and ill kept. The water runs white and fast near Gideon. Red Onkobra clay is a known product of the marsh.

The Padomaic is the great ocean on the eastern coast of Black Marsh. The old Argonians say that the Hist once ruled a far larger land. That it sank into the Padomaic in the Dawn Era. Black Marsh is the small corner left standing. Archon and the north-eastern coast face the water.

Riverwalk is a halt in a sheltered sea cove, a short way east of Thorn. It grows no food of its own. It feeds the boat crews and gives each crew a bunk. Boats tie up at a ferry stage out in the cove. A walk of planks leads there from the shore houses.

Root Talk is the council of Helstrom, a convocation of tree-minders and naheesh. It governs the city by consensus. No single voice rules. The sacred croaks that the naheesh carry are called by the same name.
The Root-Whisper are a tribe of Murkmire whose Hist withdrew after a plague. Its tree lies asleep and does not speak to the tribe. The Cyrodilic Collections helped the tribe rise again.

The Rootworm Waykeepers look after the routes of the rootworms, the great worms that carry passengers and freight through the roots. The pockets of air along them. They are a small order. Their routes are secret. A rootworm station stands at Helstrom.
The Salt-Teeth are pirates who sail inside the Reed-Sail Compact. Their boats carry the Compact's name, so a boat that looks honest may be a raider's.

The Sealed Vault is a stone undercroft beneath a ruined works. The people who found what had grown in it nailed the door shut two hundred years ago. Their note is still nailed there. A creature is shut inside. The province has bad memories of that creature.

Shadowfen is the north-western region of Black Marsh, around Stormhold. It borders Morrowind to the north and Cyrodiil to the west. It is a fetid mire of winding channels, ruined temples and Hist trees. The Legion and the Dunmer slavers have fought over it. The Great Burn started there.

A Shadowscale is an Argonian born under the sign of the Shadow. The child was taken at birth and trained to kill for Sithis. A grown Shadowscale could join the Brotherhood of assassins or leave to serve the marsh as an arbiter. A Shadowscale may not kill another Shadowscale. The order is dying out. Few remain.
Soulrest is the old Imperial capital of Black Marsh, on the south-west coast where Topal Bay meets the Southern Sea. It was the capital in the Third Era. Today the city is contested.
The Southern Sea is the water south of the marsh. Lilmoth and Soulrest are the only two cities of the province that stand on it. Oliis Bay and Topal Bay are both parts of it.

The Sul-Xan are a cult of the Naga that takes souls. They wear jade death masks and sacrifice outsiders and Argonians alike. They follow only the cruellest part of the Argonian faith and scorn the rest as weakness. Every tribe fears them.

The Sunken Archive is an order of scholars who argue over who owns knowledge. Argonians learn magic as a folk skill, with no guild of their own. So the Archive works between the local custodians of old things and the foreign mages of the Synod and the College of Whispers.

The Synod is a chartered order of mages and a rival of the College of Whispers. Both grew from the Mages Guild, which broke apart at the start of the Fourth Era. The Synod forbids necromancy and does not share what it learns freely. It has no hall in Argonia, but it hunts for artefacts of power here through buyers.
Tear is a Dunmer border town on the coastal plain just north of the saltrice country. The Tear road reaches it from Thorn. House Dres ran its slave trade from Tear for centuries.
The Empty Cradle is the name of the order of the Shadowscales. The masters who gave it its orders are gone. Three buyers now bid for what is left of its work.

The Thorn Ash-Reed Accord is the body on the northern border that argues over title to the saltrice fields. It also argues over what the border remembers, the raids of House Dres and the grievances of the Dunmer quarter. It has a magistracy, a militia hall and a counting floor.
Umbriel is a flying city. In 4E 48, it came up out of the south and destroyed Lilmoth. It killed much of the south of the province.

The Umbriel Witness Society is a body of people who argue over how the year 4E 48 should be remembered. Some of them want a complete record of every account. Others want a memorial place that is not disturbed. The Society has its archive in Lilmoth.

The Unbound Root is a movement that puts the Hist above every law. Its people say that the Hist shape an Argonian's body and mind. That the state uses that bond to demand obedience. Some of them are victims of the state's abuse. Some are fanatics. Its preachers say that real change needs a way to sever the bond.

A cutting is a piece taken from a Hist and planted away from the tree. The Unbound Root takes cuttings from a Hist. The Many-Root Conclave sees that each tree is asked for its consent. The Root takes its cuttings without asking.

A xanmeer is a stepped stone pyramid built by the old Argonians. Most are ruins now. Each had a chamber for its tribe's Hist. The insides are mazes of traps and relics. Their defences still work after thousands of years.
The Xit-Xaht are a tribe of Murkmire. Their Hist directs them. The other tribes fear them. They still build in stone, as the old Argonians did.
